questions.q: What does ROW_NUMBER() assign to each row?
options: A unique, sequential integer based on the order specified inside OVER()
A random number
The row's total count of NULL values
The same number to every row in the result set
questions.explain: 1, 2, 3, and so on, following the ORDER BY inside OVER().

questions.q: Why does ROW_NUMBER() require an ORDER BY inside OVER()?
options: ORDER BY is optional and rarely used with ROW_NUMBER
Without an order, 'which row is first' is undefined
It's only required when PARTITION BY is also present
ROW_NUMBER() ignores ORDER BY entirely
questions.explain: Unlike AVG()/COUNT() from Lesson 79, ROW_NUMBER() needs a defined sequence to assign numbers meaningfully.

questions.q: What happens when PARTITION BY is combined with ROW_NUMBER()'s ORDER BY?
options: The numbering restarts at 1 for each partition/group
It causes a syntax error
The numbering continues across all partitions without restarting
PARTITION BY is ignored when ROW_NUMBER() is used
questions.explain: This is exactly the mechanism Lesson 51 used — each duplicate group gets numbered 1, 2, 3 independently.

questions.q: Does ROW_NUMBER() ever assign the same number to two tied rows?
options: Yes, tied rows always get the same number
No — it always produces unique numbers, even for rows tied on the ORDER BY column
ROW_NUMBER() cannot be used with columns that might tie
Only when PARTITION BY is omitted
questions.explain: One of two tied rows arbitrarily gets a lower number — RANK() and DENSE_RANK() (Lesson 81) handle ties differently.

questions.q: In Lesson 51's deduplication query, what does a RowNum greater than 1 indicate?
options: The row is a duplicate of an earlier row within the same PARTITION BY group
The row is the original, unique copy
Nothing meaningful — RowNum values above 1 are ignored
The row has a NULL value in it
questions.explain: This is the exact technique explained fully now that ROW_NUMBER() and OVER()/PARTITION BY have both been covered properly.
